subject: history
title: Interpreting Cold War Blame Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll weigh who started the Cold War — and judge sources from both sides of the Iron Curtain.
meta_desc: GCSE History — interpretations of who was to blame for the Cold War.
final_note: You weighed orthodox, revisionist and post-revisionist views on Cold War blame.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The orthodox view dominated in the West for decades.

It says Stalin broke the Yalta agreement, used salami tactics to seize Eastern Europe, and blockaded Berlin. The USA only acted to contain Soviet aggression.

From the 1960s revisionist historians argued the USA was to blame.

They point to the atomic bomb, the Marshall Plan as economic empire-building, and Truman's tough talk at Potsdam. Stalin, they say, only wanted security after losing 27 million in WWII.

Most historians now take a post-revisionist view.

Both sides genuinely feared each other. The Long Telegram and Novikov Telegram show mirror-image suspicions. Ideology and misreading each other's motives made conflict almost certain.

The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.

Ideological incompatibility plus mutual suspicion after WWII — disputes over Eastern Europe, the atomic bomb, and broken wartime agreements.

mcqs.q: What did the Truman Doctrine commit the US to in 1947?
options: It began when the USSR shot down a US spy plane.
Supporting free peoples resisting communist takeover — initially Greece and Turkey — formalising the policy of containment articulated by George Kennan.
The Truman Doctrine declared war on the Soviet Union.
The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.

mcqs.q: Why did Stalin blockade West Berlin in 1948?
options: To force the Western Allies out of Berlin in response to the merging of their zones, introduction of the Deutschmark, and creation of a separate West German state.
It began when the USSR shot down a US spy plane.
Stalin blockaded Berlin to stop Nazis escaping to the West.
Stalin blockaded Berlin because he wanted to invade Western Europe.
